title: Sandboxed Telemetry & Retention Proposal for POC
summary: Working draft proposing a sandbox-first telemetry and retention approach for customer POCs; includes recommended retention tiers, redaction/obfuscation patterns, a lightweight DPA addendum draft paragraph set, and a workshop agenda for customer review.
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working proposal for how we handle telemetry, logs, and minimal persisted artifacts during customer POCs (proofs-of-concept). Target audience: solutions engineering, customer security reviewers, and legal (DPA discussion). Goal: enable rapid evaluation while minimizing customer data exposure and keeping customers comfortable with short-term telemetry retention and access controls.

Context and assumptions:
- POCs are short-lived (typically 2–8 weeks) and should avoid long-term retention of unsanitized customer inputs.
- Customers will be evaluating model behavior, latency/cost, and integration pathways; we need observability for debugging but it must be scoped.
- Many customers require: no plaintext storage of PII, ability to run in a sandbox/VPC or with a token-filtering proxy, and clear retention windows.

High-level proposal (sandbox-first):
1) Default POC mode: sandbox-only telemetry. All telemetry from the customer’s environment flows through a short-lived sandbox proxy layer we maintain for the POC. The proxy performs deterministic redaction and optional hashing for identifiers. Logs retained by Redwood are limited to what is necessary to reproduce issues (traces, model responses, low-fidelity metadata).
2) Synthetic-data-first option: before ingesting live customer traffic, run a 48–72h synthetic dataset exercise to validate prompts and response formats. This reduces triage time later and decreases need for sensitive data collection.
3) Customer-controlled private mode: if customer insists on private deployment for POC, require a signed minimal DPA addendum covering temporary telemetry retention and agreed retention tiers (see "Proposed retention tiers" below).

Telemetry categories and handling rules:
- Request payloads (full): default = not stored. Transiently visible in memory for in-flight debugging; if a customer grants explicit permission, we can store small, white-listed examples (max 10) with manual redaction.
- Instrumentation/metrics (timings, token counts): stored at service-level (no request payload), retained for 90 days for cost/latency analysis. Aggregated only by default.
- Debug traces (stack traces, internal errors): retained 30 days, scrubbed of payloads. Access logged and limited to named engineers.
- Audit logs (configuration changes, who accessed what): retained 180 days (customer-visible on request).
- Minimal repro artifacts (prompt + model response): retained only if explicitly approved, default 7 days, encrypted at rest with KMS.

Proposed retention tiers (recommended defaults for POCs):
- Ephemeral (0–24 hours): raw request bodies allowed only in in-memory traces for immediate debugging, then discarded. Use for first 48 hours only with customer opt-in.
- Short session (7 days): sanitized repro excerpts and non-PII metadata; useful for reproducing issues during active POCs.
- Analytics (90 days): aggregated metrics and derived usage tables for cost and perf trending. No raw text.
- Audit/legal (up to 7 years): only for enterprise customers with regulatory need — requires explicit clause in DPA addendum and may be stored in customer-managed logs.

Redaction & obfuscation patterns (implementation notes):
- Deterministic hashing for stable identifiers (e.g., user_id -> sha256 with salt). Salt is per-customer and may be customer-provided (preferred).
- PII detection pipeline: lightweight regex-first pass (emails, SSNs, credit card patterns) + optional ML-based recognizer for names/addresses. When detected, redact to token type (e.g., <EMAIL_REMOVED>) and store a hash of original only when customer opts in.
- Token filtering proxy: introduce a small sidecar service that customers run in their network (or we provide as docker image) that filters/strips tokens before reaching Redwood. Default configuration strips: bearer tokens, passwords, long hex sequences.
- Prefix/truncation policy: for long inputs (>2k tokens) we store only the last 512 and first 256 tokens for debugging to limit exposure and still allow context repro.

Access controls and operational constraints:
- Role-based access: only named SE engineers and on-call SREs can access scrubbed repro artifacts; access requires a short justification and is logged.
- Time-limited elevated access: temporary access (max 8 hours) can be requested; all actions audited.
- Encryption: data at rest encrypted with AES-256; keys managed by Redwood KMS in hosted POC by default. For sensitive customers we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for POCs run in VPC/dedicated mode.
- Region constraints: for customers with regional requirements, we propose running the sandbox proxy in the requested region; if not possible, provide a summary of telemetry retained and commit to deleting regionally restricted artifacts within 48 hours after POC end.

Draft DPA addendum language (POC-focused, short):
NOTE: the below is a draft paragraph set intended to be a starting point for legal review and customer negotiation.
1) "Purpose and Scope — The Parties agree that during the POC the Provider will collect and process telemetry and limited logs solely for the purpose of providing support, troubleshooting, and evaluating the Service. The scope of processing will be limited to aggregate performance metrics, transient debug traces, and sanitized repro artifacts as set out in the POC Data Handling Schedule."
2) "Retention — Unless otherwise agreed in writing, raw request payloads containing customer-submitted content will not be persisted by Provider. Provider may retain sanitized reproductions (as defined in the POC Data Handling Schedule) for a default period of seven (7) calendar days. Aggregated metrics may be retained for up to ninety (90) calendar days. Audit logs may be retained up to one hundred eighty (180) calendar days."
3) "PII and Redaction — Provider will apply deterministic redaction and hashing for identifiers and will not attempt to deanonymize hashed identifiers. Provider will not use customer textual inputs to train or improve models during the POC without explicit written consent."
4) "Access and Audit — Access to any retained POC artifacts will be strictly limited to named personnel and will require a documented justification; all access will be audit-logged. Customer may request deletion of retained artifacts at any time during or after the POC, and Provider will comply within forty-eight (48) hours of receipt of a valid request."

Workshop agenda for customer security/SE session (60–90 min suggested):
- 5 min: Introductions and POC objectives
- 10 min: High-level telemetry flows and sandbox overview (diagram walk-through)
- 15 min: Retention tiers and sample timelines (what we store, where, and for how long)
- 10 min: Redaction demo and sample repro artifacts (show before/after)
- 10 min: DPA addendum walkthrough and negotiation points
- 10 min: Customer deployment choices (sandbox proxy vs on-prem sidecar vs VPC)
- 10–20 min: Q&A and action items

Open questions / decision points for customer and internal teams:
- Do we offer salt management by customer for all hashing by default, or only on request? (security prefers customer-managed salt)
- For POCs with heavy debugging needs, can we agree to a temporary 48h extended retention of raw payloads with explicit approval? How to capture approval auditable?
- Any regional constraints that would prohibit running our sandbox proxy in the customer’s preferred cloud region? If yes, propose a sidecar option.

Operational checklist (pre-POC):
- Customer signs the POC DPA addendum (draft attached).
- Enable sandbox proxy endpoint in requested region (if available) or provide sidecar image.
- Default telemetry redaction rules applied in proxy.
- Provide the customer with a short checklist to configure salt, KMS preference, and data retention window.
- Kick off synthetic-data run before live traffic.

Sample small-scale runbook for incident repro (private notes for SEs):
- Step 1: reproduce locally with sanitized example from customer (use synthetic run results).
- Step 2: if reproduction fails, request ephemeral access to 1–3 raw requests (signed approval required) — log request in Jira SE-XXXX.
- Step 3: after investigation, redact and delete raw artifacts; update the customer with root-cause and retained sanitized repro.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: customer accidentally sends high-sensitivity PII during POC. Mitigation: default to synthetic-data-first and require explicit opt-in for raw storage; proxy filters high-risk patterns and alerts customer.
- Risk: developers inadvertently access raw content. Mitigation: mandatory access justification + automated deletion + two-person approval for any raw artifact retention beyond 24 hours.

Appendix A — Example redaction table (examples):
- "alice@example.com" => "<EMAIL_REMOVED>"
- "acct_0x23a...f" => "<HEX_REMOVED>"
- "John Smith, 555-1212" => "<NAME_REMOVED>"
- user_id:  "user-12345" => stored as "user-hash-<sha256>" (customer-provided salt)

Appendix B — Minimal POC DPA addendum (short form for engineering review):
- Addendum title: "POC Data Handling Addendum — Sandbox Mode"
- Key bullets: limited purpose; default ephemeral retention; no model training; customer right to delete; KMS options; named access list.

Next steps and owners:
- Priya Singh: finalize synthetic-data checklist and provide sidecar docker image by 2026-03-15.
- Evan Park: produce a short demo of redaction rules and a before/after sample by 2026-03-20.
- Legal (Sofia Martinez): run the DPA addendum draft by Legal and prepare version for initial customer review by 2026-03-22.
- SE lead (Rahul Menon): schedule a 60-min workshop with the customer and capture regional constraints by 2026-03-25.

Notes-to-self / rough ideas for improvements in future iterations:
- Consider building a "repro token" that maps a stored repro to the exact inputs (kept only in customer-controlled vault).
- Investigate a lightweight on-device redaction library to push more filtering to the customer side.
- Create a small telemetry UI in Console that surfaces only aggregated metrics for POCs to reduce need for artifact access.

End of working draft.

Unresolved: exact auditable approval flow for elevated raw-access and whether enterprise legal will accept 7-day default retention without additional contractual language.
